lines: When action enters will and rulership, what is
entered and ruled is called iṣyamāṇa, īśyamāṇa —
two kinds: ra by mere light, la by rest, the pair
being light-and-stopped. The willed is not distinct
like the external — in distinctness would lie its own
making; nor will nor rulership stands distinct:
from non-distinctness only hearing holds for ra and la,
l4.sanskrit_cite: yadā tu icchāyām īśane ca karma anupraviśati yat tat iṣyamāṇam īśyamāṇam iti ca ucyate tadā asya dvau bhedau prakāśamātreṇa raśrutiḥ viśrāntyā laśrutiḥ ralayoḥ prakāśastambhasvabhāvatvāt iṣyamāṇaṃ ca na bāhyavat sphuṭam sphuṭarūpatve tad eva nirmāṇaṃ syāt na icchā īśanaṃ vā ataḥ asphuṭatvāt eva śrutimātraṃ ralayoḥ na vyañjanavat sthitiḥ

reads_against.argmap: When karma enters icchā-īśana, what results? → Action-in-will bifurcates into ra/la uttara-varṇas whose nature is prakāśa-stambha: heard-not-expressed, hence śruti-mātra.
c1_essence: Action entering will and rulership births iṣyamāṇa/īśyamāṇa: ra by mere light, la by rest — heard, not expressed.
